title: Guardrails for policy-propagation bounce and KV cache mismatch causing cross-region reroutes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a regional capacity contraction on 2025-10-30 we observed a traffic oscillation and cross-region reroute loop that resulted in elevated latency and increased token costs. The observable failure mode combined three contributing factors: (1) a policy-propagation edge case where updated routing decisions left inconsistent TTLs across routers, (2) sticky variant affinity persisted across failover resulting in requests pinned to incompatible model variants, and (3) a KV cache namespace collision between quantized and float model variants which caused generation validation failures and triggered additional failovers. The combination amplified retry storms between regions and exhausted burst capacity for two hours.
timeline: 2025-10-30 02:12 UTC — first increase in 5xx and token latency observed on SLO dashboard (region-us-west).
2025-10-30 02:18 UTC — automation initiated fallback to shadow variant; rapid variant swaps begin.
2025-10-30 02:25 UTC — cross-region reroute loop detected, traffic oscillating between us-west and eu-west.
2025-10-30 02:40 UTC — incident declared; on-call routed to routing and runtime teams.
2025-10-30 03:10 UTC — temporary mitigation: slowed route-change propagation and enforced per-route cooldown, stabilizing traffic after 20 minutes.
2025-10-30 04:15 UTC — incident mitigated; full normal traffic by 05:00 UTC after rolling back a recent policy mesh change.
root_causes: policy propagation allowed TTL reset on partial mesh updates leading to asymmetric precedence across routers
sticky affinity tokens were not validated against target variant compatibility during failover
KV cache key schema reused same namespace for quantized and float variants causing cache poisoning and validation errors
no circuit-breaker on rapid variant swap rate; retries amplified failover behavior
action_items: (A) Implement version-handshake check before applying sticky-variant affinity: ensure client-side affinity tokens include model-compat metadata and reject affinity if mismatch detected — owner: Marco Ruiz — due: 2025-11-17
(B) Add propagation checksum and per-policy sequence number to routing mesh updates so routers can detect and reject partial/older updates — owner: Linh Tran — due: 2025-11-24
(C) Introduce route-change cooldown with exponential backoff and a short global throttling token to prevent thrash on simultaneous policy flips — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2025-11-14
(D) Separate KV cache namespaces and add variant-type scoping to keys; add automated cache-invalidation migration for existing keys — owner: Sophie Chen — due: 2025-11-30
(E) Add a circuit-breaker on variant swap rate per route (alerting and automatic pause with fallback to last-known-good variant) — owner: Marco Ruiz — due: 2025-11-21
(F) E2E staging test: simulate region capacity contraction + variant incompat changes using chaos harness and validate runbook procedures — owner: SRE team (oncall rotation) — due: 2025-12-05
(G) Instrument new metrics: variant_swap_rate, propagation_staleness, affinity_rejections, kv_cache_collision_rate; add dashboards and paging alerts — owner: Observability team — due: 2025-11-10
(H) Update runbook: explicit rollback knob for policy mesh and add step to disable sticky affinity during cross-region failover window — owner: Incident Response — due: 2025-11-07
decisions: Prioritize non-invasive telemetry and circuit-breaker work first to lower immediate risk (items E and G).
KV cache namespace separation will be performed as a migration rather than an in-place rename to avoid additional instability during rollout.
Rollouts for policy propagation checksum will target canary at 10% of routers, with 30-minute observation windows before wide rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Rollback complexity for policy mesh checksum: mitigate by having a feature-flagged rollout and a clear backward-compatibility window.
Cache migration risk: mitigate with read-through compatibility mode for 24 hours and traffic-based throttle to avoid stampeding invalidations.
Alert fatigue from new metrics: mitigate by iterating thresholds from staging and only paging on sustained 15-minute breaches.
comments: 2025-11-03 — Aisha: Created ticket following postmortem review. Assigned to Marco for immediate telemetry and breaker work.
2025-11-05 — Marco: Started spike for variant_swap_rate metric; local simulation reproduces oscillation with repeated policy flips. Linking simulation notebook.
2025-11-07 — Priya: Implemented route-change cooldown prototype in staging; observed 4x reduction in swap churn during simulated policy flaps.
2025-11-09 — Sophie: KV namespace migration plan drafted; requires a short compatibility layer. Blocking on review from runtime team.
2025-11-10 — Linh: Checksum approach vetted with small canary; no mismatches observed in 72-hour short canary. Preparing wider rollout plan.
notes: Customer impact was concentrated on mid-size customers with cross-region routing enabled; enterprise customers with dedicated pools were unaffected.
We chose to avoid immediate aggressive global rollbacks to prevent cascading failovers; instead applied localized cooldowns which stabilized the mesh faster.
Follow-up: incorporate variant-compat checks into SDK token issuance to reduce server-side affinity rejections over time.
